Science.title: Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years
Science.summary: Medications taken years or even long ago may leave lasting changes in your gut microbiome, according to a study of more than 2,500 people. Researchers discovered that common drugs, including antidepressants, blood pressure medications, and anxiety treatments, can leave microbial “fingerprints” long after patients stop taking them. Surprisingly, some anxiety medications had effects comparable to broad-spectrum antibiotics.

By focusing specifically on these two conditions, the study offers a clearer understanding of a potentially serious connection between metabolic health and brain health.

Science.title: A mysterious gap hints at black holes born from stars that never exploded

A surprising pattern in 257 black hole mergers suggests these mysterious stellar disappearances could explain the origins of a large population of black holes throughout the universe.

Science.title: A 194-year-old tortoise has a remarkable anti-aging secret hidden in its DNA

Researchers identified 287 unique genetic variants linked to processes that help repair damaged DNA, control inflammation, regulate insulin, and suppress cancer.

Culture.title: Hark! Errollyn Wallen’s glittering nativity opera A Christmas Miracle is a credit to Britten’s community vision
Culture.summary: Orford church, Suffolk Performed in the venue where Noye’s Fludde premiered and based on the same text, this festive new work shines with exuberant young performers, distinctive singalongs, lustrous designs and the spirit of mucking in When Benjamin Britten wrote Noye’s Fludde, he essentially invented community opera. Bringing professionals together with enthusiastic local amateurs, everyone mucking in to play, sing and make sets and costumes, isn’t only great fun; done right, it fosters a love of music-making that can last a lifetime. Such projects, the composer declared with his best socialist hat on, created works that were “useful to the living”. For decades, Britten contemplated a nativity opera, which somehow never transpired. Now, Errollyn Wallen , Master of the King’s Music, has filled the gap. A Christmas Miracle, co-produced by Mahogany Opera and Britten Pears Arts, sets texts from the same Chester mystery plays that inspired Noye’s Fludde, and premiered in the Orford church that Britten chose in 1958. Culture.title: Interpol and Bloc Party review – two of 00s indie’s most revered acts go toe-to-toe
Culture.summary: Utilita Arena Cardiff Kele Okereke has a tough challenge selling Bloc Party’s trite latest album – a far cry from Interpol’s ‘masterpiece’ eighth record, performed here to darkly hypnotic effect Try as one might to resist comparison, the balance of this particular yin and yang has been shifting for some time. Twelve months ago, when Interpol and Bloc Party announced a UK and European co-headline tour, the pairing looked like an even contest: two of 00s indie’s most revered acts, whose landmark debuts remain touchstones of the era. Since then, their fortunes have diverged. As an opening bass drone strafes the room, Bloc Party arrive in Cardiff in superficially fine, if puzzling, form. Their seventh album, Anatomy of a Brief Romance, has been met with diminishing returns, its Snapchat-caption triteness – “Every day is such a vibe”, runs one refrain – and creative inertia doing little to win over listeners. Culture.title: Secrets, squabbles and laughs as a Jamaican family mourns in modern classic Nine Night
Culture.summary: Kiln theatre, London Exquisitely acted, and directed with lightness and depth, Natasha Gordon’s tragicomedy about a matriarch’s wake is moving without a hint of mawkishness The death of a parent has a way of blowing up the lives of family members it leaves behind. The combustions of grief, greed and secrets revealed around a barely buried coffin litter the tragicomic works of playwrights such as Tracy Letts (August: Osage County) and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins (Appropriate). You might want to add Natasha Gordon’s debut play to that canon, although it comes wrapped in its own distinct cultural tradition. Its structure revolves around the Caribbean funeral ritual that commemorates the death of a loved one over nine nights. A debut play written by a young Black British woman, featuring an almost entirely Black British cast, it got a huge reaction at the National Theatre in 2018 . Continue reading...
